tabular_sota_test_auroc.interpretation: Tabular SOTA ceiling for the 2,000-patient MIMIC-IV cohort: the strongest classical pipeline (RandomForest/XGBoost ensemble with Gaussian augmentation). Defines the practical performance ceiling on this task and feature set.

stacked_best_auroc.interpretation: Best final fusion pipeline: few-shot probabilities + RandomForest probabilities + ETHOS embeddings → Logistic Regression meta-learner. Closes the gap to within 0.002 of the tabular SOTA ceiling.

fewshot_best_auroc.interpretation: Best few-shot sub-model alone (GFA attention + cross-attention prototypes + Proto-MAML adaptation). Reaches 0.670; the gap to the ceiling motivates the stacked/hybrid pipeline.

exp1_random_forest_auroc.interpretation: Random Forest under the strict Exp1 comparison protocol. Demonstrates the strength of tree-based models on tabular clinical data.

exp1_logreg_auroc.interpretation: Logistic Regression baseline under Exp1; included for completeness.

exp1_xgboost_auroc.interpretation: XGBoost baseline under Exp1; weaker than RF on this sample (default tuning); SOTA pipeline retunes XGBoost separately.

exp1_proposed_fewshot_auroc.interpretation: Proposed_FewShot under the strict Exp1 protocol. Episodic evaluation; not directly comparable to the stacked BEST AUROC. Demonstrates the limit of raw few-shot on tabular clinical data.

exp1_standardnn_auroc.interpretation: Standard MLP baseline; weaker than RF/LR on tabular features as expected.

exp1_federatednn_no_fewshot_auroc.interpretation: Federated MLP without the few-shot head.

federated_centralized_auroc.interpretation: Centralized training of the federated-NN architecture used in Exp3 (lower than RF because the federated architecture is intentionally simple).

federated_federated_auroc.interpretation: FedAvg-trained variant of the same architecture across 5 disease-defined nodes.

federated_auroc_gap.interpretation: Performance cost of federation (centralized − federated). On this simulation the privacy cost is approximately 0.005 AUROC, i.e. very small relative to the architecture itself.

ethos_rf_hybrid_auroc.interpretation: ETHOS embeddings concatenated with tabular features and fed to RandomForest. Demonstrates that learned token representations are useful when combined with classical models.

exp4_full_model_auroc.interpretation: Ablation baseline (full ETHOS few-shot pipeline under the ablation protocol).

exp4_no_symptom_tokens_auroc.interpretation: Ablation paradox documented in PROJECT_AUDIT_REPORT.md §13 Risk 1: when the episodic token pathway is removed, the model relies on raw tabular features which are naturally well-suited to tree-based modelling. This confirms that the bottleneck is the episodic few-shot objective on tabular data, not the symptom tokenization itself — and motivates the hybrid/stacked design.

scientific_positioning: Healthcare data is sensitive, noisy, limited, distributed, and hard to centralize.
Few-shot learning is attractive because labelled clinical data is limited.
Federated learning matters because hospitals cannot freely share raw patient data.
Symptom tokenization helps structure clinical signals.
Classical tabular models (RF, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) remain strong on structured clinical data.
Raw few-shot under-performing classical ML is not a failure; it is a scientifically valuable finding.
The strongest practical direction is hybrid clinical intelligence: classical ML + few-shot representation learning + federated/privacy-aware deployment.
